description: Transparent participatory foresight becomes a public-interest institutional capability.
Models dashboards and expert systems shape decisions with limited participation.
Private actors define technology labor infrastructure and market futures around profit and control.
Climate futures integrate historical responsibility adaptation loss and damage Indigenous rights and intergenerational ethics.
Hybrid risk and security foresight expand surveillance militarization and border-control logic.
AI systems rapidly generate forecasts classifications and scenarios for institutions.
Communities youth workers Indigenous peoples migrants and civil society challenge dominant future narratives.
Institutions prioritize immediate political financial or strategic incentives while long-term harm deepens.
